questions.question: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All spoons are forks. All forks are knives. No knife is a spatula. Conclusions: I. Some knives are spoons. II. No fork is a spatula. III. Some spoons are spatulas.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:
All spoons are forks.
All forks are knives.
No knife is a spatula.

Conclusions:
I. Some knives are spoons.
II. No fork is a spatula.
III. Some spoons are spatulas.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. Some knives are spoons. - True (because All spoons are forks, and All forks are knives. So, Some knives are spoons too)

II. No fork is a spatula. - True (because All forks are knives and No knife is a spatula. So, No fork is a spatula it is true)

questions.question: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 125 ÷ 5 + 1809 × 9 – 14 = ?
questions.questionHtml:
What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged?
125 ÷ 5 + 1809 × 9 – 14 = ?
questions.solution:
Given equation: 125 ÷ 5 + 1809 × 9 – 14 = ?

After interchanging the signs then:

⇒ 125 × 5 - 1809 ÷ 9 + 14 = ? ⇒  125 × 5 - 201 + 14 ⇒ 625 - 201 + 14
⇒ 639 - 201 = 438

questions.question: 61 is related to 18 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 213 is related to 38. To which of the following is 509 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.questionHtml: 61 is related to 18 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 213 is related to 38. To which of the following is 509 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.solution:
The logic follows here is:

Logic: n3 - 3 & n2 + 2

Now,

61 is related to 18

→ 43 - 3 = 64 - 3 = 61,

→ 42 + 2 = 16 + 2 = 18.

213 is related to 38

→ 63 - 3 = 216 - 3 = 213,

→ 62 + 2 = 36 + 2 = 38.

Similarly, for 509

→ 83 - 3 = 512 - 3 = 509,

→ 82 + 2 = 64 + 2 = 66.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question: If A is the sister of B, C is the daughter of A, D is the sister of A and E is the brother of C. How is D related to E?
questions.questionHtml: If A is the sister of B, C is the daughter of A, D is the sister of A and E is the brother of C. How is D related to E?
questions.solution:
A is the sister of B, C is the daughter of A, D is the sister of A and E is the brother of C.

​

So, D is the "Mother's sister" of E.
